title: SBJ Gaming: Preparing for League of Legends Worlds
summary: SBJ Gaming: Preparing for League of Legends Worlds  Sports Business Journal
content:
EA Sports College Football does a pretty good job capturing the experience of watching college football. Against USC, the band plays almost as much as it does at an actual game!

What weighs a ton and is cheesier than my jokes? The amount of pizzaCall of Dutyfans ate during the 2024 Call of Duty League championship at the Credit Union of Texas Event Center in Allen, about 30 miles north ofdowntown Dallas.

“We did the math on it, per slice that was sold, and it was literally a ton of pizza sold that weekend,” said Ross Girouard, the Event Center’s assistant GM.

Girouard and his crew ended up buying more fixings for pizza for that event. When it comes to hosting esports audiences, the folks running food and beverage and logistics can count on fans who eat and spend a lot. This time, they’re planning on more pizza — well, more of everything, really — when the Event Center hosts legs of theLeague of Legends Worlds 2026 championshipfor more than two weeks: the Swiss Stage (Oct. 23-26 and Oct. 28-31), quarterfinals (Nov. 3-6) and semifinals (Nov. 7-8). It’ll be the longest esports event for the arena, putting to the test everything staff have learned about hosting competitive gaming tournaments since 2019’s Overwatch League visit.

“We didn’t really know exactly what we were getting into and how that particular opportunity might present itself in others ways in future years,” said Bill Herman, the Event Center’s GM. “And that was a great event we had back then. And we were planning on doing another major event in 2020. And unfortunately, that got canceled due to COVID. And then coming out of that, it took a little while, like everything else related to COVID, to get our legs back under us again.”

The next major esports event for the Event Center was 2024’s Call of Duty championship. Event Center staff kept up with the evolving needs of competitive gaming when it comes to tech deployments and resources, along with following other trends in putting on such events, to build on their learnings from the OWL visit.

title: Hanwha Life Esports Defeats kt Rolster to Reach 17 Wins, Secures Playoff and Worlds Spots
summary: Hanwha Life Esports Defeats kt Rolster to Reach 17 Wins, Secures Playoff and Worlds Spots  invenglobal.com
content:
Hanwha Life Esports defeated kt Rolster 2-1 in their 2026 LoL Champions Korea (LCK) regular season Round 4 Legend Group match, held at LoL PARK in Jongno on the 15th. With today's victory, Hanwha Life Esports has secured its spot in both the playoffs and the World Championship.

kt Rolster took the lead by securing the first set. The tone was set early; 'Perfect' Lee Seung-min's K'Sante dodged a three-man gank from Hanwha Life Esports with flashy footwork and even managed to take down 'Zeka' Kim Geon-woo's Ryze, who had dived under the tower. kt Rolster then swept five kills in a one-sided skirmish triggered by a Dragon contest.

'Bdd' Kwak Bo-seong, playing Syndra, disrupted Hanwha Life Esports at critical moments with precise Scatter the Weak plays. Around the 23-minute mark, Hanwha Life Esports attempted to catch the Syndra in the dark, but her calm reaction and the quick arrival of her teammates led to the deaths of Hanwha Life's mid and jungle. kt Rolster capitalized on the play by securing Baron.

Empowered by the Baron buff, kt Rolster pushed into the top lane. Despite fierce resistance from Hanwha Life Esports—which resulted in a chaotic fight where everyone except 'Effort' Lee Sang-ho's Bard fell—the outcome remained unchanged. Leveraging their momentum, kt Rolster secured both Baron and the Ocean Soul, demonstrating a clear power gap as they destroyed the Nexus to take the first set.

Hanwha Life Esports took the lead in the second set. 'Zeka's' Akali picked up three early kills and began to snowball rapidly. Having seized control, Hanwha Life Esports repeatedly forced skirmishes to widen the gap. The fed Akali even secured a solo kill against 'Zeus' Choi Woo-je's Rumble in the side lane.

By the 23-minute mark, the global gold lead had reached 10k. During a standoff in kt Rolster's jungle, 'Kanavi' Seo Jin-hyeok's Vi boldly initiated a teamfight in a narrow corridor. Hanwha Life Esports poured out overwhelming damage, resulting in a decisive victory and securing the second set.
